Thanks for the ping — digging in. Quick summary of what I'm seeing from runtime metrics and recent config rollouts:

Investigation notes:
- This tenant pool is on a mixed-mode lane where we recently increased batching aggressiveness (smaller per-request overhead) last week for cost savings.
- The combination of tightened per-batch slot accounting + an overly-aggressive hot-key eviction policy has created slot starvation for several hot prefixes. Requests for those prefixes are queuing, which widens batching windows and causes downstream HOL (head-of-line) blocking in the GPU scheduler.
- When the KV cache misses spike, the runtime falls back to heavy compute, which bubbles up as p99 spikes and transient 5xx when compute lanes saturate.

Immediate mitigation (I will orchestrate now):
1) Temporarily relax slot accounting for the affected tenant pool (increase max-slots-per-batch by 30%) — should reclaim capacity within ~5m.
2) Disable the recent hot-key eviction change for that pool and increase the hot-key TTL to reduce evictions.
3) Short-term: lower the batching hold timeout from 25ms to 12ms for the route to reduce tail latency at slight throughput cost.

I'll push changes to the canary pool first and monitor metrics (p99, 5xx, KV eviction rate). If we see improvement within 10–15m on canary, we'll roll to the rest. Marcus, please stand by for exec communication if needed.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
